title: Set each vine row's end anchor in line, as far out as the row's end post is tall
instruction: Set the brace anchor for each of the two vine rows. Each row has a tall end post nearest you and a shorter line post beyond it, and the row's line runs through the centres of its two posts. Stand one grey anchor block upright on each row's line, past its end post on the side away from the line post, with the block's centre as far from the end post's centre as that end post is tall. The two end posts are different heights.
context: Vineyard and orchard crews (farmworkers, O*NET 45-2092) build and repair trellis end assemblies. A row's end post carries the pull of all the row's wires, so it is held back by a brace wire running from its top down to an anchor set in the ground in line with the row, beyond the end post. A common rule of thumb in trellis guides is to set the anchor as far from the end post as the post stands above ground, so the brace runs at about 45 degrees: set closer, the steep brace has to pull much harder and drives the post down; set farther, the anchor takes headland the tractor needs to turn. Rows on different trellis systems have end posts of different heights, so each row's distance is read from its own end post, not from the shorter line posts. Nothing is marked: the worker sights along the row's posts to extend its line past the end post and measures out along it. At this 1:12 scale the 150 mm post stands for 1.8 m.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Two short vine rows at about 1:12 scale and two anchor blocks; nothing is marked on the table. (1) Four posts: dark weathered-wood square posts, 25 x 25 mm (thicker than scale, so they show in the top photo), fixed upright to the table, each turned so that two of its sides run along its row. Left row: end post 100 mm tall centred at x 32.0 cm, y +20.0 cm; line post 80 mm tall centred at x 44.6 cm, y +16.6 cm. Right row: end post 150 mm tall centred at x 37.0 cm, y -18.0 cm; line post 130 mm tall centred at x 49.6 cm, y -21.4 cm. In each row the line post stands 126 mm farther from the arms and 34 mm further right than the end post (130.5 mm apart, centre to centre) and is 20 mm lower, so the two rows are parallel and run forward and to the right at 15.1 degrees to x. (2) Two trellis wires: light-grey galvanised steel, represented by 5 x 5 mm fixed bars 104.5 mm long, one along each row between its two posts' facing sides, 70 mm above the table (below both posts' tops). (3) Two anchor blocks: loose grey cast-concrete blocks, 30 x 30 mm and 40 mm tall, 80 g, standing upright on a 30 x 30 mm face with their sides parallel to x and y, centred at x 15.0 cm, y +33.0 cm (in front of the left arm) and x 15.0 cm, y -33.0 cm (in front of the right arm). The blocks are identical: either may serve either row. Nothing else is on the table. For reference (not marked): each row's line runs through the centres of its two posts; the left row's anchor point, on that line 100 mm beyond the end post's centre on the side away from the line post, is at x 22.3 cm, y +22.6 cm, and the right row's, 150 mm beyond, at x 22.5 cm, y -14.1 cm.
scoring: End state: read from where the two blocks are at the last step (in simulation from the blocks' poses). A block is 'set' when it stands on the table on one of its 30 x 30 mm faces: its lowest point within 3 mm of the table top and its 40 mm axis tilted at most 10 degrees from vertical (either end up; its heading does not matter). For a row, a block's 'offset' is the distance from its centre to the row's line (the straight line through the centres of the row's two posts), and its 'reach' is how far its centre lies beyond the end post's centre along that line, on the side away from the line post (negative beside or behind the end post). H is that row's end-post height: 100 mm on the left row, 150 mm on the right. Score 0 if either block is off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise each row scores on its own and the score is their sum; a block counts for at most one row (the blocks are matched to the rows the way that scores more). A row scores 0.5 if a set block has an offset of 10 mm or less and a reach within 10 mm of H (left 90 to 110 mm, right 140 to 160 mm); 0.25 if a set block has an offset of 20 mm or less and a reach within 15 mm of H (left 85 to 115 mm, right 135 to 165 mm); 0 otherwise (no block there, or one lying on its side, standing on the other block, held above the table, between the posts, past the line post, or farther off the line or the distance). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Every outcome: the start 0; both rows right 1.0; one right and the other as found 0.5; one right and the other within the looser band 0.75; both within the looser band 0.5; one within it and the other as found 0.25. Wrong rules score 0 for the row: blocks set straight back along x from the end posts instead of along the rows (26 mm off the left line, 39 mm off the right); the right row's 150 mm used on the left row (50 mm too far) or the left row's 100 mm on the right (50 mm short); the line posts' heights (80 and 130 mm: 20 mm short on each row); the 130.5 mm post spacing (30.5 mm too far on the left, 19.5 mm short on the right). One distance for both rows: 100 or 150 mm gets one row right (0.5); their 125 mm average is 25 mm off both (0). The trial ends early once 1.0 has held with both blocks still (centre moving less than 5 mm in all over the last 0.5 s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, lay a straightedge on the table against the same side face of both of a row's posts (their sides run along the row): it is parallel to the row's line, 12.5 mm from it, and runs on past the end post. Read the block's centre square off it, and tape its distance along it from the end post's centre.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. Posts and wires are fixed boxes; the posts stand upright (real end posts often lean a little toward their anchor). A real anchor is screwed or buried and a brace wire runs from the end post's top to it; here a loose block marks the anchor's spot, with no brace wire. Scale about 1:12. The scorer sees only the blocks: a block held still standing on the table counts as set; success needs both still for 3 s, longer than letting go takes.
reset_notes: Stand both anchor blocks back upright on their starting spots at x 15.0 cm, y +33.0 cm and x 15.0 cm, y -33.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. The posts and wires are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
